newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia noon rubber down, awaits INRO intervention.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia noon rubber down, awaits INRO intervention.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices were down at midday and traders were hoping for support from the International Natural Rubber Organisation (INRO) if the rates fall to an intervention level set by the group.
INRO's daily indicator price was at 184.89 Malaysian/Singapore cents a kg on July 4, compared to 186.82 on July 3. The 5-day moving average was at 190.03, against 192.43 previously.
Under INRO's intervention guidelines, 183 cents is the level which the group "may buy" rubber in the market.
"Technically, they should come in at this level, but then they may wait for the must buy level," said a trader. INRO's "must buy" is at 172 cents.

At midday, the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board quoted August buyers of the benchmark RSS1 at 241 Malaysian/Singapore cents (95 U.S. cents) a kg, down two cent from Friday's close. August SMR20 was a cent off to 236.50.

At noon, trading houses offered the SMR20 at 234, SMR10 at 236, SMR5 at 247, SMR CV at 304, SMR L at 285 and drum latex at 202. Traders said on Friday they expect prices for each grade to fall by at least five cents this week.
